168.subject: Botany
168.text:
Assertion : Nucleus is the controlling centre of a cell.
Reason: Pores in the nuclear envelop regulate the flow of materials in and out of the nucleus.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
168.sol:
Nucleus is the controlling centre of a cell as it contains chromosomes and genes. Chromosomes contain the DNA which by transcription prepare RNA which in turn leads to the formation of proteins by translation. These proteins regulate the various metabolic processes going in the cell. Besides this, nucleus contains genetic information for reproduction, development \& behaviour of an organism.
 Nuclear membrane is double layered, semipermeable and is perforated by minute, circular nuclear pores. The pore controls the passage of macromolecules like tRNAs, mRNAs, ribosomal proteins, enzymes etc. during different processes of transcription, translation etc.
168.meta: Assertion : Nucleus is the controlling centre of a cell. Reason: Pores in the nuclear envelop regulate the flow of materials in and out of the nucleus.

1970.text: Chemosensitive area of respiratory centre in medulla is affected by
1970.sol: Human beings have a significant ability to maintain and moderate the respiratory rhythm to suit the demands of the body tissues. A specialised centre present in the medulla region of the brain called respiratory rhythm centre is primarily responsible for this regulation. A chemosensitive area is situated adjacent to the rhythm centre which is highly sensitive to $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and hydrogen ions. Increase in these substances can activate this centre, which in turn can signal the rhythm centre to make necessary adjustments in the respiratory process.

1994.subject: Zoology
1994.text: Assertion : Oxytocin is also known as Antidiuretic hormone $(\mathrm{ADH})$.Reason : Oxytocin can cause an increase in the renal reabsorption of water.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
1994.sol:
(d): It is not oxytocin, but the hormone vasopressin (also known as antidiuretic hormone, $\mathrm{ADH}$ ) because it reduces the volume of urine by increasing the reabsorption of water from the urine in the distal convoluted tubules, collecting tubules and collecting ducts in the kidney. It does so by rendering the walls of those tubules permeable to water. Failure of secretion of vasopressin leads to a reduced renal reabsorption of water and a consequent elimination of a large volume of very dilute (hypotonic) urine.
Oxytocin is another hormone released by the posterior lobe of pituitary gland. Oxytocin contracts the mammary glands, smooth muscles of uterus. Uterine contractions, stimulated by oxytocin at the end of pregnancy, help in the child-birth or parturition, hence also called birth hormone. The oxytocin - induced contractions of the mammary gland muscles help in the flow of stored milk from the mammary glands, hence also called milk ejection hormone.
1994.meta: Assertion : Oxytocin is also known as Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) . Reason : Oxytocin can cause an increase in the renal reabsorption of water.

2081.subject: Zoology
2081.text:
Assertion : Parturition is induced by neural signal in maternal pituitary.
Reason : At the end of gestation period, the maternal pituitary releases prolactin which causes uterine contractions.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
Ifboth assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
2081.sol:
The process of delivery of the foetus (childbirth) is called parturition. Parturition is induced by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism. The signals for parturition originate from the fully developed foetus and the placenta which induce mild uterine contractions called foetal ejection reflex.
This triggers release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary. Oxytocin acts on the uterine muscles and causes stronger uterine contractions, which in turn stimulate further secretion of oxytocin. The stimulatory reflex between the uterine contractions and oxytocin secretion continues resulting in stronger and stronger contractions. This leads to expulsion of the baby out of the uterus through the birth canal.

5329.subject: Chemistry
5329.text: If the mole fraction of ethanol in a solution of ethanol in water is 0.050 , then find the molarity of the given solution.
5329.sol:
Moles of ethanol $=0.050$
Moles of water $=1-0.050=0.95 \mathrm{ mol}$.
Mass of ethanol $=0.05 \times 46=2.3 \mathrm{ g}$.
Mass of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}=0.95 \times 18=17.1 \mathrm{ g}$
Mass of solution $=2.3+17.1 \mathrm{ g}=19.4 \mathrm{ g}$
Assuming, density of water $=1 \mathrm{ g} / \mathrm{mL}$
Volume of solution $=\frac{\text{ Mass of solution }}{\text{ Density }}=19.4 / 1=19.4 \mathrm{ mL}=0.0194 \mathrm{ L}$
Molarity of solution $=\frac{\text{ Number of moles of ethanol }}{\text{ Volume of solution (L) }}=\frac{0.050}{0.0194}=2.57 \cong 2.8 \mathrm{M}$

$⇒ a^{2} - 4b = b^{2} - 4a$

$⇒ $\left(a - b\right)\left(a + b\right)$ + 4 $\left(a - b\right)$ = 0$

$⇒ $\left(a - b\right)\left(4 + a + b\right)$ = 0$

$⇒ a + b + 4 = 0$

11610.sol:
Let \(x=(1+y)^n-1=n y\)
\(\begin{aligned}
+ & \frac{n(n-1)}{2 !} y^2+\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3 !} y^3+\ldots \ldots \ldots . . \\
& =\frac{2}{5}+\frac{1.3}{2 !}\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^2+\frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3 !}\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^3+\ldots \ldots \ldots . . .
\end{aligned}\)
On comparing first three terms, we get
\(n y=\frac{2}{5}, \frac{n(n-1)}{2 !} y^2=\frac{1 \cdot 3}{2 !}\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^2\)
and \(\quad \frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3 !} y^3=\frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3 !}\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^3\)
From first two relations, we get
\($\begin{array}{rlrl} 
& & \frac{n y(n y-y)}{2 !} & =\frac{\frac{2}{5}\left(\frac{2}{5}-y\right)}{2 !}=\frac{1 \cdot 3}{2 !}\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^2 \\
\Rightarrow \quad & \left(\frac{2}{5}\right)-y & =1 \cdot 3\left(\frac{2}{5}\right) \\
\Rightarrow & & y & =\frac{2}{5}-\frac{6}{5}=-\frac{4}{5} \text{$ and $} n=-\frac{1}{2}
\end{array}$
Now, on putting \(n=-\frac{1}{2}\) and \(y=-\frac{4}{5}\) in LHS of third relation, we get
\(\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{1}{2}-1\right)\left(-\frac{1}{2}-2\right)}{3 !}\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right)^3 \\
& =\frac{\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1+2}{2}\right)\left(\frac{1+4}{2}\right)}{3 !} 2^3\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^3=\frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3 !}\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^3=\text{ RHS }
\end{aligned}\)
So, \(x=\left(1-\frac{4}{5}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}-1=\sqrt{5}-1\) so, \(\frac{1}{x}=\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}\)
So, \(x+\frac{1}{x}=\sqrt{5}-1+\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}=\frac{5 \sqrt{5}-3}{4}\)
Hence, option (d) is correct.

16039.text: The maximum force acting on a particle executing simple harmonic motion is \(10 \mathrm{~N}\). The force on the particle when it is midway between mean and extreme positions will be
16039.sol:
Maximum force on the particle performing SHM, \(F_{\max }=10 \mathrm{~N}\)
We know that, In SHM, when body is at maximum displacement (amplitude \(a\)), then force on the particle is maximum.
\(\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad F_{\max }=\text{ mass } \times \text{ acceleration }=m \cdot \alpha_{\max } \quad {\left[\therefore \alpha_{\max }=\omega^2 a\right]} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 10=m \cdot \omega^2 a \Rightarrow 10=m a \omega^2 \quad \ldots(\mathrm{i})
\end{aligned}\)
Force on the particle when it is mid way \(\left(y=\frac{a}{2}\right)\) between mean and extreme position,
\(\begin{aligned}
& F=m \omega^2 y=m \omega^2 \cdot\left(\frac{a}{2}\right) \quad\left[\because y=\frac{a}{2}\right] \\
& =\frac{\operatorname{ma\omega }^2}{2}=\frac{10}{2} \quad \text{ [from Eq. (i)] } \\
& =5 \mathrm{~N} \\
\end{aligned}\)

17758.text:
What is the stoichiometric coefficient of $\mathrm{SO}_2$ in the following balance reaction?
$\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}(a q)+\mathrm{SO}_2(g) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}(a q)+\mathrm{HSO}_4^{-}(a q)$

Oxidation half reaction:
$\mathrm{SO}_2(\mathrm{ g})+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(l) \longrightarrow \mathrm{HSO}_4^{-}(a q)+3 \mathrm{H}^{+}(a q)+2 e^{-}...(i)$
Reduction half reaction:
$\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}(a q)+8 \mathrm{H}^{+}+5 e^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}(a q)+4 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(l)...(ii)$
Multiply eq. (i) by 5 and (ii) by 2 and then add
$\begin{aligned}
2 \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}(a q)+5 \mathrm{SO}_2(g) & +2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(l)+\mathrm{H}^{+}(a q) \\
& \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Mn}^{+}(a q)+5 \mathrm{HSO}_4^{-}(a q)
\end{aligned}$
Thus, the stoichiometric coefficient of $\mathrm{SO}_2$ in the above balance equation is 5.

20863.subject: Chemistry
20863.text:
5.0 moles of an Ideal gas at 3.0 atm pressure and $27^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ is compressed isothermally to half its volume by application of an external pressure of $3.5 \mathrm{ atm}$. What is the amount of work done (in joules) on the gas?
Given: $1 \mathrm{ L} \mathrm{ atm}=101.3 \mathrm{ J}: \mathrm{R}=0.082 \mathrm{ L} \mathrm{ atm} \mathrm{ K}{ }^{-1} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$
20863.sol:
The initial state of the gas is given by $n = 5.0$ mol, $P_1 = 3.0$ atm, and $T = 27^{{}^{\circ}}C = 300$ K.

Using the ideal gas law $PV = nRT$, the initial volume $V_1$ is calculated as:

$V_1 = \dfrac{nRT}{P_1} = \dfrac{5.0 \times 0.082 \times 300}{3.0} = 41$ L.

The gas is compressed isothermally to half its volume, so the final volume $V_2$ is:

$V_2 = \dfrac{V_1}{2} = \dfrac{41}{2} = 20.5$ L.

The change in volume $\Delta V = V_2 - V_1 = 20.5 - 41 = -20.5$ L.

The work done on the gas during an irreversible isothermal compression against a constant external pressure $P_{ext}$ is given by $W = -P_{ext} \Delta V$.

Given $P_{ext} = 3.5$ atm, the work done is:

$W = -3.5 \times (-20.5) = 71.75$ L atm.

Converting the work into Joules using the conversion factor $1$ L atm $= 101.3$ J:

$W = 71.75 \times 101.3 = 7268.275$ J.

Rounding to one decimal place, the work done is $7268.3$ J.

Answer: 7268.3

21388.subject: Mathematics
21388.sol:
Given $f(x) = \left(\dfrac{3+x}{1+x}\right)^{2+3x}$. Taking the natural logarithm on both sides:

$\ln f(x) = (2+3x) \ln \left(\dfrac{3+x}{1+x}\right) = (2+3x) [\ln(3+x) - \ln(1+x)]$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{1}{f(x)} f'(x) = 3 [\ln(3+x) - \ln(1+x)] + (2+3x) \left[\dfrac{1}{3+x} - \dfrac{1}{1+x}\right].

At $x=0$, $f(0) = $\left(\dfrac{3}{1}\right)^$2 = 9$.

Substituting $x=0$ into the derivative expression:

\dfrac{1}{f(0)}$f'(0) = 3 [\ln 3 - \ln 1] + (2) $\left[\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{1}\right]$.

$\dfrac{1}{9} f'(0) = 3 \ln 3 + 2 \left[\dfrac{1-3}{3}\right] = 3 \ln 3 + 2 \left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = 3 \ln 3 - \dfrac{4}{3}$.

$f'(0) = 9 \left(3 \ln 3 - \dfrac{4}{3}\right) = 27 \ln 3 - 12$.

Answer: $-12+27 \log 3$

21461.subject: Mathematics
21461.text: If $2 f \left(x^2\right)+3 f \left(\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)=$x^2-1, \forall x \in R-\{0\}$, then f\left(x^8\right) is equal to$
21461.sol:
Given the equation $2 f(x^2) + 3 f\left(\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right) = x^2 - 1$.

Let $t = x^2$. Then the equation becomes $2 f(t) + 3 f\left(\dfrac{1}{t}\right) = t - 1$ for all $t > 0$.

Replacing $t$ with $\dfrac{1}{t}$, we get $2 f\left(\dfrac{1}{t}\right) + 3 f(t) = \dfrac{1}{t} - 1$.

We have a system of two linear equations in $f(t)$ and $f\left(\dfrac{1}{t}\right)$:
1) $2 f(t) + 3 f\left(\dfrac{1}{t}\right) = t - 1$
2) $3 f(t) + 2 f\left(\dfrac{1}{t}\right) = \dfrac{1}{t} - 1$

Multiply equation (1) by 2 and equation (2) by 3:
$4 f(t) + 6 f\left(\dfrac{1}{t}\right) = 2t - 2$
$9 f(t) + 6 f\left(\dfrac{1}{t}\right) = \dfrac{3}{t} - 3$

Subtracting the first from the second:
$5 f(t) = \dfrac{3}{t} - 3 - (2t - 2) = \dfrac{3}{t} - 2t - 1 = \dfrac{3 - 2t^2 - t}{t} = -\dfrac{2t^2 + t - 3}{t} = -\dfrac{(2t + 3)(t - 1)}{t} = \dfrac{(1 - t)(2t + 3)}{t}$.

Therefore, $f(t) = \dfrac{(1 - t)(2t + 3)}{5t}$.

Substituting $t = x^8$ into the expression for $f(t)$:
$f(x^8) = \dfrac{(1 - x^8)(2x^8 + 3)}{5x^8}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\left(1-x^8\right)\left(2x^8+3\right)}{5x^8}$

21886.subject: Mathematics
21886.text:
Three bags contain a number of red and white balls are as follows.
Bag I: 3 red balls
Bag II: 2 red balls and 1 white ball
Bag III: 3 White balls
The probability that bag $i$ will be chosen and a ball is selected from it is $\dfrac{i}{6}, i=1,2,3$. if a white ball is selected, what is the probablity that it came from Bag III
21886.sol:
Let $B_1, B_2, B_3$ be the events of choosing Bag I, Bag II, and Bag III respectively. Let $W$ be the event of selecting a white ball.

The probabilities of choosing the bags are given by $P(B_1) = \dfrac{1}{6}$, $P(B_2) = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}$, and $P(B_3) = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

The conditional probabilities of selecting a white ball from each bag are:
$P(W|B_1) = \dfrac{0}{3} = 0$
$P(W|B_2) = \dfrac{1}{3}$
$P(W|B_3) = \dfrac{3}{3} = 1$

Using the law of total probability, the probability of selecting a white ball is:
$P(W) = P(B_1)P(W|B_1) + P(B_2)P(W|B_2) + P(B_3)P(W|B_3)$
$P(W) = \left(\dfrac{1}{6} \times 0\right) + \left(\dfrac{2}{6} \times \dfrac{1}{3}\right) + \left(\dfrac{3}{6} \times$1\right)$
$P(W) = 0 + $\dfrac{2}{18} + \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{2 + 9}{18} = \dfrac{11}{18}

Using Bayes' theorem,$ the probability that the white ball came from Bag III is:
P(B_3|W) = $\dfrac{P(B_3)P(W|B_3)}{P(W)}
$P(B_3|W) = $\dfrac{\dfrac{3}{6} \times$ 1}{$\dfrac{11}{18}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{18}{11} = \dfrac{9}{11}

Answer: \dfrac{9}{11}$

Given $P(B) = \dfrac{3}{5}$, $P(A|B) = \dfrac{1}{2}$, and $P(A \cup B) = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

Using the definition of conditional probability, $P(A \cap B) = P(A|B) \times P(B) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{3}{10}$.

Using the addition rule $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$, we have $\dfrac{4}{5} = P(A) + \dfrac{3}{5} - \dfrac{3}{10}$.

$P(A) = \dfrac{4}{5} - \dfrac{3}{5} + \dfrac{3}{10} = \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{3}{10} = \dfrac{2+3}{10} = \dfrac{5}{10} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

The expression to evaluate is $P(A \cup B)' + P(A' \cup B)$.

$P(A \cup B)' = 1 - P(A \cup B) = 1 - \dfrac{4}{5} = \dfrac{1}{5}$.

Using the property $P(A' \cup B) = P(A' \cap B')' = 1 - P(A' \cap B')$. By De Morgan's Law, $A' \cap B' = (A \cup B)'$, so $P(A' \cup B) = 1 - P((A \cup B)') = 1 - (1 - P(A \cup B)) = P(A \cup B) = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

Alternatively, $P(A' \cup B) = P(A') + P(B) - P(A' \cap B) = (1 - P(A)) + P(B) - (P(B) - P(A \cap B)) = 1 - P(A) + P(A \cap B) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{10} = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{10} = \dfrac{5+3}{10} = \dfrac{8}{10} = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

Summing the two parts: $\dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{4}{5} = 1$.

Answer: 1

22086.subject: Mathematics
22086.text: If the mean of $4,7,2,8,6$ and $k$ is 7. Then the mean deviation from the mean of these observations is
22086.sol:
The mean of the observations $4, 7, 2, 8, 6, k$ is given as $7$.

$\dfrac{4 + 7 + 2 + 8 + 6 + k}{6} = 7$

$\dfrac{27 + k}{6} = 7$

$27 + k = 42$

$k = 42 - 27 = 15$

The observations are $4, 7, 2, 8, 6, 15$. The mean is $\bar{x} = 7$.

The mean deviation from the mean is given by $\dfrac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} |x_i - \bar{x}|$.

Mean deviation $= \dfrac{|4-7| + |7-7| + |2-7| + |8-7| + |6-7| + |15-7|}{6}$

Mean deviation $= \dfrac{|-3| + |0| + |-5| + |1| + |-1| + |8|}{6}$

Mean deviation $= \dfrac{3 + 0 + 5 + 1 + 1 + 8}{6} = \dfrac{18}{6} = 3$.

Answer: 3

22665.subject: Physics
22665.text:
The variation of the stopping potential (V_0$) with the frequency of incident radiation(n) is as given below.
[n_0$ - threshold frequency. h- Planck's constant e- electronic charge] then the slope of the graph AB with the frequency axis is:
22665.sol:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is given by:

$K_{\text\max} = hn - \Phi$

where $h$ is Planck's constant, $n$ is the frequency of incident radiation, and $\Phi$ is the work function of the metal.

We know that $K_{\text\max} = eV_0$, where $e$ is the charge of an electron and $V_0$ is the stopping potential. Substituting this into the equation, we get:

$eV_0 = hn - \Phi$

$V_0 = \left(\dfrac{h}{e}\right)n - \dfrac{\Phi}{e}$

Comparing this equation with the standard equation of a straight line $y = mx + c$, we have:

$y = V_0$
$x = n$
Slope, $m = \dfrac{h}{e}$

Therefore, the slope of the graph of stopping potential ($V_0$) versus frequency ($n$) is $\dfrac{h}{e}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{h}{e}$

23084.subject: Physics
23084.text: The magnetic susceptibility of an ideal diamagnetic substance is
23084.sol:
A diamagnetic substance is characterized by the property of being repelled by a magnetic field. The magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ is defined by the relation $M = \chi H$, where $M$ is the magnetization and $H$ is the magnetic field intensity.

For a perfectly diamagnetic substance, the interior magnetic field $B$ is zero, which implies $B = \mu_0(H + M) = 0$.

This leads to $M = -H$.

Substituting this into the definition of susceptibility, we get $\chi = \dfrac{M}{H} = \dfrac{-H}{H} = -1$.

Answer: $-1$

23982.subject: Chemistry
23982.text: What is the order of bond energy between C=S $\ $ C=Te, and between Cl–Cl $\ $ F–F?
23982.sol:
The bond energy of C=S is greater than that of C=Te because the $2p$-$3p$ orbital overlap in C=S is more effective than the $2p$-$5p$ orbital overlap in C=Te. As the size of the bonded atom increases, the extent of overlap decreases, leading to a weaker bond.

The bond energy of Cl-Cl is greater than that of F-F. Although F is smaller and expected to form a stronger bond, the extremely small size of the F atom results in strong interelectronic repulsions between the lone pairs on the two bonded F atoms. This repulsion weakens the F-F bond compared to the Cl-Cl bond.

Thus, C=S > C=Te and Cl-Cl > F-F.

Answer: C=S > C=Te and Cl–Cl > F–F

On Differentiating both sides,
$$
\begin{aligned}

\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\Rightarrow \frac{x f^{\prime}(x)-f(x)}{x^2}=1 \Rightarrow \frac{d}{d x}\left\{\frac{f(x)}{x}\right\}=1
$$
On integrating both sides,
$$
\begin{array}{ll} 
& \frac{f(x)}{x}=x+C \quad\left[\because f(1)=\frac{1}{3}\right] \\
\Rightarrow \quad & \frac{1}{3}=1+C \Rightarrow \quad C=-\frac{2}{3} \\
& \text { Now, } \quad f(x)=x^2-\frac{2}{3} x \\
\Rightarrow \quad & f(2)=4-\frac{4}{3}=\frac{8}{3}
\end{array}
$$
Note Here, $f(1)=2$ does not satisfy given function.
$$
\therefore \quad f(1)=\frac{1}{3}
$$
For that, $f(x)=x^2-\frac{2}{3} x$ and $\quad f(2)=4-\frac{4}{3}=\frac{8}{3}$

26556.subject: Physics
26556.text: Most materials have the refractive index, $n>1$. So, when a light ray from air enters a naturally occurring material, then by Snell's law, $\frac{\sin \theta_{1}}{\sin \theta_{2}}=\frac{n_{2}}{n_{1}}$, it is understood that the refracted ray bends towards the normal. But it never emerges on the same side of the normal as the incident ray. According to electromagnetism, the refractive index of the medium is given by the relation, $\mathrm{n}=c / v=\pm \sqrt{\varepsilon_{r} \mu_{r}}$, where $c$ is the speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum, $v$ its speed in the medium, $\varepsilon_{r}$ and $\mu_{r}$ are the relative permittivity and permeability of the medium respectively. In normal materials, both $\varepsilon_{r}$ and $\mu_{r}$, are positive, implying positive $n$ for the medium. When both $\varepsilon_{r}$ and $\mu_{r}$ are negative, one must choose the negative root of $n$. Such negative refractive index materials can now be artificially prepared and are called metamaterials. They exhibit significantly different optical behavior, without violating any physical laws. Since $n$ is negative, it results in a change in the direction of propagation of the refracted light. However, similar to normal materials, the frequency of light remains unchanged upon refraction even in meta-materials. Question: Choose the correct statement.
options: The speed of light in the meta-material is $v=c|n|$
The speed of light in the meta-material is $v=\frac{c}{|n|}$
The speed of light in the meta-material is $v=c$.
The wavelength of the light in the meta-material $\left(\lambda_{m}\right)$ is given by $\lambda_{m}=\lambda_{\text{air }}|n|$, where $\lambda_{\text{air }}$ is wavelength of the light in air.
26556.sol:
Speed of light in a medium, $V=\frac{C}{n}$ $n$ for meta-material $=|n|$

$\therefore \quad$ Speed of light in the meta-material $V=\frac{C}{|n|}$.

After time $T, L=$ constant

Given below are two statements :
Statement I: The number of pairs among $[Al_2O_3, Cr_2O_3]$, $[Cl_2O_7, Mn_2O_7]$, $[Na_2O, V_2O_3]$ and $[CO, N_2O]$ that contain oxides of same nature (acidic, basic, neutral or amphoteric) is $4$.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

Statement I:
$Al_2O_3$ and $Cr_2O_3$ are both amphoteric oxides.
$Cl_2O_7$ and $Mn_2O_7$ are both acidic oxides.
$Na_2O$ and $V_2O_3$ are both basic oxides.
$CO$ and $N_2O$ are both neutral oxides.
All $4$ pairs contain oxides of the same nature. Hence, Statement I is true.

Statement II:
$Na_2O$ is a strongly basic oxide.
$Al_2O_3$ is an amphoteric oxide.
$CO$ is a neutral oxide.
$Cl_2O_7$ is a strongly acidic oxide.
Thus, the most basic oxide is $Na_2O$ and the most acidic oxide is $Cl_2O_7$. Hence, Statement II is true.

Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

28677.text:
$\left[\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{PPh}_{3}\right)_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{2}\right]$ is a paramagnetic complex. Identify the INCORRECT statements about this complex.
A. The complex exhibits geometrical isomerism.
B. The complex is white in colour.
C. The calculated spin-only magnetic moment of the complex is 2.84 BM .
D. The calculated CFSE (Crystal Field Stabilization Energy) of Ni in this complex is $-0.8 \Delta_{\mathrm{o}}$.
E. The geometrical arrangement of ligands in this complex is similar to that in $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
28677.sol:
In $[Ni(PPh_3)_2Cl_2]$, Nickel is in $+2$ oxidation state. $Ni^{2+}$ has a $3d^8$ electronic configuration.
The complex is given as paramagnetic. For a 4-coordinate $d^8$ system, paramagnetism implies a tetrahedral geometry ($sp^3$ hybridization) with two unpaired electrons.
Statement A: Tetrahedral complexes of the type $[MA_2B_2]$ do not exhibit geometrical isomerism because all positions are adjacent to each other. Thus, A is incorrect.
Statement B: Most $Ni(II)$ complexes are colored due to $d-d$ transitions. $[Ni(PPh_3)_2Cl_2]$ is a dark blue/green crystalline solid, not white. Thus, B is incorrect.
Statement C: With 2 unpaired electrons, the spin-only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{2(2+2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83$ BM. Thus, C is correct.
Statement D: For a tetrahedral complex with $d^8$ configuration, the CFSE is calculated as $CFSE = [(-0.6 \times 4) + (0.4 \times 4)]\Delta_t = -0.8\Delta_t$. The statement mentions $-0.8\Delta_o$, which is incorrect as the complex is tetrahedral, not octahedral. Thus, D is incorrect.
Statement E: $Ni(CO)_4$ is a tetrahedral complex ($sp^3$ hybridization). Since $[Ni(PPh_3)_2Cl_2]$ is also tetrahedral, their geometrical arrangements are similar. Thus, E is correct.
The incorrect statements are A, B, and D.

30979.subject: Chemistry
30979.text:
Correct statements from the following are:
A. Nitrogen in oxidation states from $+1$ to $+4$ disproportionates in acid medium.
B. Nitrogen has the ability to form $d\pi - p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself and other elements with small size and high electronegativity.
C. N-N single bond is stronger than P-P single bond.
D. Nitrogen has highest density in its group due to small size.
E. The maximum covalency of nitrogen is four since it has only four valence orbitals for bonding.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
30979.sol:
Statement A is correct. Nitrogen in oxidation states from $+1$ to $+4$ tends to disproportionate in acidic medium. For example, $3HNO_2 \rightarrow HNO_3 + H_2O + 2NO$.

Statement B is incorrect. Nitrogen does not have d-orbitals in its valence shell, so it cannot form $d\pi - p\pi$ multiple bonds. It forms $p\pi - p\pi$ multiple bonds.

Statement C is incorrect. The N-N single bond is weaker than the P-P single bond due to high interelectronic repulsion between the non-bonding electrons, which arises from the small N-N bond length.

Statement D is incorrect. Density increases down the group in group 15. Nitrogen is a gas and has the lowest density in its group, while bismuth has the highest.

Statement E is correct. Nitrogen has only four valence orbitals (one 2s and three 2p orbitals) available for bonding. Therefore, its maximum covalency is restricted to four.

Thus, only statements A and E are correct.

Answer: A and E Only

31640.subject: Chemistry
31640.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : 1,2,3-Trihydroxypropane can be separated from water by simple distillation.
Statement (II) : An azeotropic mixture cannot be separated by fractional distillation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
31640.sol:
Statement I: $1,2,3$-Trihydroxypropane (glycerol) has a very high boiling point (around $290^{\circ}\text{C}$) and it decomposes at its boiling point under normal atmospheric pressure. Therefore, it cannot be separated from water by simple distillation. Instead, it is separated by distillation under reduced pressure (vacuum distillation). Hence, Statement I is false.

Statement II: An azeotropic mixture is a constant boiling mixture in which the liquid and vapour phases have the exact same composition. Because there is no change in composition upon boiling, the components of an azeotropic mixture cannot be separated by fractional distillation. Hence, Statement II is true.

Therefore, Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

Answer: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

32996.text: If a right circular cone, having maximum volume, is inscribed in a sphere of radius $3cm$, then the curved surface area (in ${cm}^{2}$) of this cone is :
32996.sol:
In $△ AMC, AM = 3sin2\theta \text{ and } MC = 3cos2\theta$

$V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi{r}^{2}h$ where, $r$ is radius and $h$ is height of cone

$⇒ V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi{\left(3sin ⁡ 2\theta\right)}^{2}\left(3 + 3cos2\theta\right)$

(since, radius of cone $= AM$ and height of cone $= MC$)

$⇒ V = \pi\left(36\sin^{2} ⁡ \theta\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta\right)\left(2\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta\right)\left[∵ sin ⁡ 2\theta = 2sin ⁡ \thetacos ⁡ \theta \text{ and } cos ⁡ 2\theta = 2\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta - 1\right]$

$= 72\pi\sin^{2} ⁡ \theta\cos^{4} ⁡ \theta$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $\theta$, we get

$\dfrac{dv}{d\theta} = 72\pi\left[2sin ⁡ \theta\cos^{5} ⁡ \theta - 4\sin^{3} ⁡ \theta\cos^{3} ⁡ \theta\right]$

For maximum value, $\dfrac{dV}{d\theta} = 0$

$⇒ 72\pi\left[2sin ⁡ \theta\cos^{5} ⁡ \theta - 4\sin^{3} ⁡ \theta\cos^{3} ⁡ \theta\right] = 0 ⇒ \tan^{2} ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Thus, volume is maximum when $tan ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Hence, curved surface area $S = \pirl$

$= \pir\sqrt{{\left(3 + 3cos ⁡ 2\theta\right)}^{2} + {( 3sin ⁡ 2\theta )}^{2}}\left[∵ l = \sqrt{{r}^{2} + {h}^{2}}\right]$

$= \pi\left(3sin ⁡ 2\theta\right)\sqrt{36\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta} = 18\pi\left(2sin ⁡ \theta\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta\right)$

$= 36\pi\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} . \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{24\pi}{\sqrt{3}} = 8\sqrt{3}\pi$

34761.text: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + {e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 2\right)y = \left({x}^{2} - 2x\right)\left({x}^{2} - 2\right){e}^{2x}$ and $y\left(0\right) = 0$, then the value of $y\left(2\right)$ is
34761.sol:
Given

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + {e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 2\right)y = \left({x}^{2} - 2x\right)\left({x}^{2} - 2\right){e}^{2x}$

It is linear differential equation so,

$IF = {e}^{∫ \left({x}^{2} - 2\right){e}^{x}dx}$

$= {e}^{{x}^{2}{e}^{x} - 2 ∫ x{e}^{x}dx - 2{e}^{x}} = {e}^{{x}^{2}{e}^{x} - 2\left[x{e}^{x} - {e}^{x}\right] - 2{e}^{x}}$

$IF = {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}}$

Now solution is given by

$y \times {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} = ∫ {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} \times \left({x}^{2} - 2x\right)\left({x}^{2} - 2\right){e}^{2x}$

$= ∫ {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} \times \left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 2\right){e}^{x}$

Now let $\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x} = t$

We get ${e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right) + {e}^{x}\left(2x - 2\right)dx = dt$

${e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 2x + 2x - 2\right)dx = dt$

${e}^{x}\left({x}^{2} - 2\right)dx = dt$

$y \times {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} = ∫ {e}^{t} \times t \times dt$

$y \times {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} = {e}^{t}\left(t - 1\right) + c$

$y \times {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} = {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}}\left(\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x} - 1\right) + c$

Now at $x = 0y = 0$

$0 \times {e}^{0} = {e}^{0}\left(0x{e}^{x} - 1\right) + c$

$0 = - 1 + c c = 1$

Putting the value of $c = 1$ we get the equation as

$⇒ y \times {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}} = {e}^{\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x}}\left(\left({x}^{2} - 2x\right){e}^{x} - 1\right) + 1$

Now putting $x = 2$ in equation we get

$y \times {e}^{\left(4 - 4\right){e}^{2}} = {e}^{\left(4 - 4\right){e}^{2}}\left(\left(4 - 4\right){e}^{2} - 1\right) + 1$

$⇒ y \times {e}^{0} = {e}^{0}\left(\left(0\right){e}^{2} - 1\right) + 1$

$⇒ y = - 1 + 1 = 0$

41060.text: At which temperature the r.m.s. velocity of a hydrogen molecule equal to that of an oxygen molecule at $47 ° C$ ?
41060.sol:
The r.m.s velocity of the molecule of a gas of molecular weight $M$ at Kelvin temperature $T$is given by, ${V}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$.

Let ${M}_{O}$ and ${M}_{H}$ are molecular weight of oxygen and hydrogen and ${T}_{O}$ and ${T}_{H}$ the corresponding Kelvin temperature at which ${V}_{r . m . s}$ is same for both,

${V}_{r . m . s} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3R{T}_{O}}{{M}_{O}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3R{T}_{H}}{{M}_{H}}}$. Hence $\dfrac{{T}_{O}}{{M}_{O}} = \dfrac{{T}_{H}}{{M}_{H}}$

${T}_{O} = 273 ° C + 47 ° C = 320K$, 

${M}_{O} = 32$, 

${M}_{H} = 2 ⇒ {T}_{H} = \dfrac{2}{32} \times 320 = 20K$

42192.subject: Physics
42192.text:
Water drops fall from a tap on the floor, 5 m below, at regular intervals of time, the first drop strikes the floor when the sixth drop begins to fall. The height at which the fourth drop will be from ground, at the instant when the first drop strikes the ground is $\_\_\_\_$ m.
$\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\right)$
42192.sol:
Time for first drop to fall 5 m:
$5 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2$ gives $t = 1$ s.
Since the first drop strikes when the sixth begins, there are 5 intervals: each interval $T = \frac{1}{5} = 0.2$ s.
When drop 1 hits the ground (at $t = 1$ s), drop 4 has been falling for $t_4 = 1 - 3 \times 0.2 = 0.4$ s.
Distance fallen by drop 4: $s_4 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times (0.4)^2 = 0.8$ m.
Height of drop 4 above ground: $5 - 0.8 = 4.2$ m.

& \Rightarrow \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{mg}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{B}}-\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{A}} \\

& \Rightarrow \sqrt{\mathrm{gR} \frac{2(\sqrt{2}+1)}{\sqrt{2}}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \\
& \Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{10 \times 14 \times 2(2.4)}{1.4}}=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}} \\
& \Rightarrow 21.9=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}}
\end{aligned}$

47013.sol:
The correct sequence is
Zygote $\rightarrow$ Cleavage $\rightarrow$ Morula $\rightarrow$ Blastula $\rightarrow$ Gastrula.
At about $30-36 \mathrm{hrs}$ after fertilisation, the zygote divides into smaller cells by a process called cleavage. It is division of cells. It results in a solid ball of cells, called morula. It is a 16 -celled stage. It forms blastula which is a 64 -celled stage. It contains a fluid-filled cavity called blastocoel. It ultimately leads to gastrula stage. It is a multilayered structure which is followed by organogenesis.

47262.subject: Biology
47262.text:
A student was asked to identify a permanent slide of mitosis. He made the following observations.
(i) Splitting of centromere and formation of daughter chromatids.
(ii) Chromatids are migrating towards the opposite poles.
The stage would be
47262.sol:
During anaphase, the centromeres split and the sister chromatids separate to form daughter chromatids.

These daughter chromatids then begin their migration towards the opposite poles of the cell due to the shortening of spindle fibres.

Metaphase is characterized by the alignment of chromosomes at the equator.

Telophase involves the decondensation of chromosomes at the poles and the reformation of the nuclear envelope.

Prophase is marked by the condensation of chromatin and the initiation of spindle formation.

Answer: Anaphase

$\begin{aligned} \quad V_{1} &=V_{2} \\ \frac{q_{1}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} r_{1}} &=\frac{q_{2}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} r_{2}} \end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}=\frac{q_{1}}{q_{2}}=\frac{15 m C}{45 m C}=\frac{1}{3}$
Final charge on first sphere,
$q_{1}=\frac{1}{3}\left(q_{1}+q_{2}\right)=\frac{1}{3} \times 60=20 \mathrm{mC}$

50409.subject: Physics
50409.text: To propagate both longitudinal and transverse waves, a material must have
50409.sol:
In transverse waves, the particle motion is normal to the direction of the wave.
Therefore, as the wave propagates each element of the medium undergoes shearing strain.
In longitudinal waves, the constituents of the medium oscillate about their mean position along the direction of wave propagation like propagation of sound wave.
This involves compressive stress (pressure). Thus, transverse waves be propagated in medium which can sustain shearing stress.
Similarly, longitudinal waves can be propagated in medium which can sustain bulk modulus.

55443.subject: Chemistry
55443.text: Which of the following molecules is capable of forming Zwitter ion?
55443.sol:
A Zwitter ion is a dipolar ion formed by the internal transfer of a proton from an acidic group to a basic group within the same molecule.

Among the given options, $\text{NH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ (glycine) is an amino acid that contains both an acidic carboxyl group ($-\text{COOH}$) and a basic amino group ($-\text{NH}_2$).

In aqueous solution, the $-\text{COOH}$ group donates a proton to the $-\text{NH}_2$ group, forming the Zwitter ion $^{+}\text{NH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^{-}$.

The other molecules lack either an acidic or a basic group required for this internal proton transfer.

Answer: $\text{NH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$

56013.subject: Chemistry
56013.text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the rate constant?
options: It is proportionality constant in rate law that relates reaction rate to reactant concentrations.
It is independent of concentration of reactant.
Greater the value of rate constant slower is the reaction.
56013.sol:
According to the rate law, the rate of a reaction is given by $\text{Rate} = k[\text{Reactants}]^{n}$.

Here, $k$ is the rate constant, which is a proportionality constant relating the reaction rate to the reactant concentrations.

The rate constant $k$ is independent of the initial concentration of the reactants but depends on the temperature as given by the Arrhenius equation $k = A e^{-E_a/RT}$.

From the rate law, it is evident that the rate of the reaction is directly proportional to the rate constant $k$. Therefore, a greater value of the rate constant implies a faster reaction, not a slower one.

Hence, the statement 'Greater the value of rate constant slower is the reaction' is incorrect.

Answer: Greater the value of rate constant slower is the reaction.

60193.text: If a particle moves such that the displacement (s) is proportional to the square of the velocity (v), then its acceleration (a) is
60193.sol:
Given $s \propto v^2$

$s = k v^2$ where $k$ is a constant.

Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{ds}{dt} = 2kv \dfrac{dv}{dt}$

Since $\dfrac{ds}{dt} = v$ and $\dfrac{dv}{dt} = a$:

$v = 2kv a$

$a = \dfrac{1}{2k}$

Since $k$ is a constant, acceleration $a$ is a constant.

Answer: a constant

60246.subject: Mathematics
60246.text: The length of the perpendicular drawn from the origin on the normal to the curve $x^2+2 x y-3 y^2=0$ at the point $(2,2)$ is
60246.sol:
The perpendicular from the origin to the normal of the curve $x^2 + 2xy - 3y^2 = 0$ at $(2,2)$ is determined.

Implicit differentiation gives the slope of the tangent at any point:
$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x + y}{3y - x}$

At $(2,2)$, the slope of the tangent is $m_t = \frac{2 + 2}{3(2) - 2} = 1$, so the slope of the normal is $m_n = -1$.

The equation of the normal is then $y - 2 = -1(x - 2)$ or $x + y - 4 = 0$.

The perpendicular distance from the origin to this line is
$\frac{|1(0) + 1(0) - 4|}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2}} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{2}} = 2\sqrt{2}$

The length is $2\sqrt{2}$ units, corresponding to option C.

60907.subject: Mathematics
60907.text: If the function $f(x) = \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}(\sin 3x + \sin x)}{2\sin 2x\sin\dfrac{3x}{2} + \cos\dfrac{5x}{2} - \cos\dfrac{3x}{2}}$ for $x \neq \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is continuous at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then the value of $f  \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)is equal to$
60907.sol:
Given the function:

$f(x) = \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}(\sin 3x + \sin x)}{2\sin 2x\sin\dfrac{3x}{2} + \cos\dfrac{5x}{2} - \cos\dfrac{3x}{2}}$

Using the sum-to-product formula $\sin C + \sin D = 2\sin\dfrac{C+D}{2}\cos\dfrac{C-D}{2}$, the numerator simplifies to:

$4\sqrt{2}(2\sin 2x \cos x) = 8\sqrt{2}\sin 2x \cos x$

For the denominator, using the formula $\cos C - \cos D = -2\sin\dfrac{C+D}{2}\sin\dfrac{C-D}{2}$, we get:

$\cos\dfrac{5x}{2} - \cos\dfrac{3x}{2} = -2\sin 2x \sin\dfrac{x}{2}$

Substituting this back into the denominator:

$2\sin 2x\sin\dfrac{3x}{2} - 2\sin 2x \sin\dfrac{x}{2} = 2\sin 2x \left(\sin\dfrac{3x}{2} - \sin\dfrac{x}{2}\right)

Using the formula \sin C - \sin D = 2\cos\dfrac{C+D}{2}\sin\dfrac{C-D}{2}, the expression inside the parenthesis becomes:

\sin\dfrac{3x}{2} - \sin\dfrac{x}{2} =2\cos x \sin\dfrac{x}{2}

So, the denominator simplifies to:

2\sin 2x (2\cos x \sin\dfrac{x}{2}) =4\sin 2x \cos x \sin\dfrac{x}{2}

Now, substituting the simplified numerator and denominator back into $ f(x)$:

$f(x) = $\dfrac{8\sqrt{2}\sin 2x \cos x}{4\sin 2x \cos x \sin\dfrac{x}{2}}

For $ x $\neq \dfrac{\pi}{2}, we can cancel \sin 2x \cos x$ from the numerator and denominator:

$f(x) = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sin\dfrac{x}{2}}

Since $ f(x)$ is continuous at $x = $\dfrac{\pi}{2}, its value at this point is equal$ to its limit as x \to$\dfrac{\pi}{2}:

$ f$\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \lim_{x \to \pi/2} \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sin\dfrac{x}{2}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} =4$

Therefore, $f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) =4 = (2)^2$.

Answer: $(2)^2$

62571.text: If $3 \sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x}{1+x^2}\right)-4 \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}\right)+2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{2 x}{1-x^2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}$, then the value of $x=$
62571.sol:
Given the equation $3 \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)-4 \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}\right)+2 \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1-x^2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}$.

Using standard identities for inverse trigonometric functions, the relevant ranges for $x > 0$ are considered.

For $0 < x < 1$:

$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)=2\tan^{-1}x$,
$\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}\right)=2\tan^{-1}x$,
$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1-x^2}\right)=2\tan^{-1}x$.

Substituting into the equation:
$3(2\tan^{-1}x)-4(2\tan^{-1}x)+2(2\tan^{-1}x)=\frac{\pi}{3}$
$2\tan^{-1}x=\frac{\pi}{3}$
$\tan^{-1}x=\frac{\pi}{6}$
$x=\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

This value satisfies $0 < x < 1$ and is valid.

For $x = 1$:

The term $\tan^{-1} \left(\frac{2}{0}\right)$ is undefined, so no solution.

For $x > 1$:

$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)=\pi-2\tan^{-1}x$,
$\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}\right)=2\tan^{-1}x$,
$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1-x^2}\right)=2\tan^{-1}x-\pi.

Substituting gives:
3(\pi-2\tan^{-1}x)-4(2\tan^{-1}x)+2(2\tan^{-1}x-\pi)=\frac{\pi}{3}
\pi-10\tan^{-1}x=\frac{\pi}{3}
10\tan^{-1}x=\frac{2\pi}{3}
\tan^{-1}x=\frac{\pi}{15}.

However, \frac{\pi}{15} < \frac{\pi}{4}, which contradicts the assumption \tan^{-1}x > \frac{\pi}{4} for $ x > 1$, so no solution in this range.

The only valid solution is $$x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}},$$corresponding to option C.

$

64935.subject: Mathematics
64935.sol:
Let $x = \dfrac{\pi}{5}$.

$5x = \pi \Rightarrow 2x = \pi - 3x$

Taking sine on both sides:

$\sin(2x) = \sin(\pi - 3x)$

$\sin(2x) = \sin(3x)$

$2\sin x \cos x = 3\sin x - 4\sin^3 x$

Since $\sin x \neq 0$, dividing by $\sin x$ gives:

$2\cos x = 3 - 4\sin^2 x$

$2\cos x = 3 - 4(1 - \cos^2 x)$

$4\cos^2 x - 2\cos x - 1 = 0$

Solving the quadratic equation for $\cos x$:

$\cos x = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 4(4)(-1)}}{2(4)} = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{20}}{8} = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{4}$

Since $x = \dfrac{\pi}{5}$ lies in the first quadrant, $\cos x > 0$.

Therefore, $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}\right) = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{4}$

65196.text: If $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}, \bar{d}$ are unit vectors such that $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}=\frac{1}{2}, \bar{c} \cdot \bar{d}=\frac{1}{2}$ and the angle between $\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$ and $\bar{c} \times \overline{\mathrm{d}}$ is $\frac{\pi}{6}$, then the value of $|[\bar{a} \overline{\mathrm{ b}} \mathrm{ d}] \bar{c}-[\bar{a} \overline{\mathrm{ b}} \bar{c}] \mathrm{d}|=$
65196.sol:
Given $E = |[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{d}] \bar{c} - [\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}] \bar{d}|$, express the scalar triple products using cross and dot products:

$E = |((\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{d}) \bar{c} - ((\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{c}) \bar{d}|$.

This matches the vector triple product identity $\bar{X} \times (\bar{Y} \times \bar{Z}) = (\bar{X} \cdot \bar{Z})\bar{Y} - (\bar{X} \cdot \bar{Y})\bar{Z}$, with $\bar{X} = \bar{a} \times \bar{b}$, $\bar{Y} = \bar{c}$, and $\bar{Z} = \bar{d}$. Thus, $E = |(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times (\bar{c} \times \bar{d})|$.

Let $\bar{P} = \bar{a} \times \bar{b}$ and $\bar{Q} = \bar{c} \times \bar{d}$. Then $E = |\bar{P} \times \bar{Q}| = |\bar{P}||\bar{Q}|\sin\phi$, where $\phi = \frac{\pi}{6}$ is given, so $\sin\phi = \frac{1}{2}$.

The magnitudes are computed similarly: $|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}| = |\bar{a}||\bar{b}|\sin\theta_1 = 1 \cdot 1 \cdot \sin(\frac{\pi}{3}) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, since $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = \frac{1}{2}$ implies $\theta_1 = \frac{\pi}{3}$.

Likewise, $|\bar{c} \times \bar{d}| = |\bar{c}||\bar{d}|\sin\theta_2 = 1 \cdot 1 \cdot \sin(\frac{\pi}{3}) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

Substituting, $E = \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{3}{8}$.

The correct answer is C.

68111.text: A horizontal pipe carries water in a streamline flow. At point along the pipe, where the cross-sectional area is $A_1$, the velocity of water is $V_1$ and the pressure is $P_1$. What is the pressure of water at another point where the cross-sectional area is $A_2$?
68111.sol:
Using the equation of continuity:

$A_1 V_1 = A_2 V_2 \Rightarrow V_2 = \dfrac{A_1 V_1}{A_2}$

Using Bernoulli's theorem for a horizontal pipe:

$P_1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\varrho V_1^2 = P_2 + \dfrac{1}{2}\varrho V_2^2$

$P_2 = P_1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\varrho (V_1^2 - V_2^2)$

Substituting the value of $V_2$:

$P_2 = P_1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\varrho \left($V_1^2 - $\dfrac{A_1^2 V_1^2}{A_2^2}\right)

$ P_2 = P_1 + $\dfrac{\varrho V_1^2}{2A_2^2}($ A_2^2 - A_1^2)

69933.text: A rigid diatomic gas undergoes adiabatic change. Its pressure P and temperature T are related as $P \propto T^x$ where x is
69933.sol:
For an adiabatic process, the relation between pressure and volume is $PV^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$.

Using the ideal gas equation $PV = nRT$, we can replace $V$ with $\dfrac{nRT}{P}$ to get:

$P \left(\dfrac{T}{P}\right)^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$

$P^{1-\gamma} T^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$

$P \propto T^{\dfrac{\gamma}{\gamma-1}}$

Comparing this with $P \propto T^x$, we get $x = \dfrac{\gamma}{\gamma-1}$.

For a rigid diatomic gas, the number of degrees of freedom is $f = 5$.

The ratio of specific heats is $\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{7}{5}$.

Substituting the value of $\gamma$ into the expression for $x$:

$x = \dfrac{\dfrac{7}{5}}{\dfrac{7}{5} - 1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{7}{5}}{\dfrac{2}{5}} = \dfrac{7}{2} = 3.5$

Answer: $3.5$

70894.subject: Biology
70894.text: Which of the following organisms has salt secreting glands?
options: Both Marine iguanas and Sea Turtles
70894.sol:
Salt-secreting glands are specialized organs found in certain marine reptiles and birds to excrete excess salt and maintain osmotic balance.

Marine iguanas possess supraorbital salt glands above their eyes, which empty into the nasal cavity and allow them to forcefully expel excess salt.

Sea turtles have modified lachrymal glands near their eyes that secrete a highly concentrated salt solution, helping them excrete salt ingested with seawater.

Marine mammals like whales do not possess salt glands. They manage excess salt primarily through highly efficient kidneys that produce concentrated urine.

Therefore, both marine iguanas and sea turtles possess salt-secreting glands.

Answer: Both Marine iguanas and Sea Turtles

70969.subject: Biology
70969.text: The pure form of water is NOT ____.
70969.sol:
Pure water ($H_2O$) undergoes auto-ionization to produce equal concentrations of hydrogen ions ($H^{+}$) and hydroxyl ions ($OH^{-}$).

At a temperature of $298\text{ K}$, the concentration of both these ions is exactly $10^{-7}\text{ M}$, which corresponds to a $\text{pH}$ value of $7$. This means that pure water is completely neutral, being neither acidic nor basic.

Furthermore, water is classified as an inorganic compound because its molecular structure does not contain carbon-hydrogen covalent bonds, and it is chemically reactive rather than completely inert.

Since pure water is inherently neutral, it is not acidic.

Answer: acidic

71013.text: In the lungs, the alveolar air is separated from blood by ______.

a layer of squamous epithelium and a layer of transitional epithelium

two layers of tunica externa, interna and tunica media
71013.sol:
The diffusion membrane in the lungs is composed of three major layers: the thin squamous epithelium of alveoli, the endothelium of alveolar capillaries, and the basement substance in between them.

The endothelium of the alveolar capillaries is also a type of simple squamous epithelium.

Therefore, the alveolar air is separated from the blood by two layers of simple squamous epithelium.

Answer: two layers of simple squamous epithelium

71257.text: The two strands in a DNA molecule are ________.
71257.sol:
The two strands of a DNA molecule are antiparallel, meaning one strand runs in the $5'$ to $3'$ direction while the other runs in the $3'$ to $5'$ direction.

They are also complementary, as the nitrogenous bases on one strand pair specifically with bases on the other strand (Adenine pairs with Thymine, and Cytosine pairs with Guanine) through hydrogen bonds.

Answer: antiparallel and complementary.

71372.text: Which one of the following is a symptom of Klinefelter's Syndrome?
71372.sol:
Klinefelter's syndrome is a genetic disorder caused by the presence of an additional copy of the X chromosome, resulting in a karyotype of 47, XXY.

Individuals with this syndrome have overall masculine development, but feminine characteristics are also expressed. One of the prominent symptoms is the development of breasts, which is known as Gynaecomastia.

Webbed neck, broad shield-shaped chest, and lower posterior hair line are symptoms associated with Turner's syndrome (45, XO).

71435.text:
Select the set of correct statements regarding ETS in aerobic respiration.
A. $F_1$ catalyses the synthesis of ATP from ADP.
B. Protons are channeled from outer chamber of mitochondria into inner chamber by $F_0$ part of oxysome.
C. Cytochrome C acts as mobile electron carrier transferring electrons from Complex V and IV.
D. Cytochrome C is a small, calcium containing protein tightly associated with inner membrane.
E. Cytochrome C acts as mobile electron carrier transferring electrons from complex III to IV.
Select the correct option
71435.sol:
Statement A is correct. The $F_1$ headpiece of ATP synthase contains the catalytic site for the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate.

Statement B is correct. The $F_0$ part of the oxysome (ATP synthase) forms a transmembrane channel that facilitates the diffusion of protons from the intermembrane space (outer chamber) to the mitochondrial matrix (inner chamber).

Statement C is incorrect. Cytochrome c transfers electrons between Complex III (Cytochrome $bc_1$ complex) and Complex IV (Cytochrome c oxidase), not Complex V.

Statement D is incorrect. Cytochrome c is a small protein attached loosely to the outer surface of the inner mitochondrial membrane, and it contains iron (in its heme group), not calcium.

Statement E is correct. Cytochrome c acts as a mobile electron carrier transferring electrons from Complex III to Complex IV.

Therefore, statements A, B, and E are correct.

Answer: A, B and E only

71551.subject: Biology
71551.text: Which type of mineral absorption shows a sudden drop when the roots are deprived of oxygen?
71551.sol:
Mineral absorption in plants can occur via passive or active processes.

Passive absorption does not require metabolic energy and includes mechanisms like direct ion-exchange, mass flow, and Donnan equilibrium. These processes are not directly dependent on oxygen availability.

Active absorption requires metabolic energy in the form of ATP, which is primarily generated through aerobic respiration. When roots are deprived of oxygen, aerobic respiration ceases, leading to a sudden drop in ATP production. Consequently, active absorption of minerals shows a sudden and significant decline.

Answer: Active Absorption.

72055.subject: Chemistry
72055.text: In which of the following changes, entropy of the system decreases?
options: Formation of liquid water from hydrogen and oxygen gas molecules
72055.sol:
Entropy is a measure of the randomness or disorder of a system.

For the dissolution of solid $\text{I}_2$ in water, a solid changes into an aqueous solution, which increases the randomness. Thus, entropy increases ($\Delta S > 0$).

For the dissociation of $\text{H}_2$ molecules into atoms, $\text{H}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{H}(g)$, the number of gaseous particles increases. Thus, entropy increases ($\Delta S > 0$).

For the formation of liquid water from hydrogen and oxygen gas molecules, $2\text{H}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$, gaseous reactants are converted into a liquid product. The number of moles of gas decreases ($\Delta n_g = -3$), leading to a decrease in randomness. Thus, entropy decreases ($\Delta S < 0$).

For the melting of ice at $0^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$, a solid changes into a liquid, which increases the randomness. Thus, entropy increases ($\Delta S > 0$).

Answer: Formation of liquid water from hydrogen and oxygen gas molecules

72297.subject: Physics
72297.text: For uniform acceleration in linear motion which of the following is NOT CORRECT?
options: The area under the velocity-time graph equals the displacement.
Acceleration is the slope of velocity-time graph.
72297.sol:
For uniform acceleration in linear motion, the acceleration $a$ is constant.

The kinematic equation for velocity is $v = u + at$, which represents a linear relationship between velocity $v$ and time $t$.

Thus, the velocity-time graph is a straight line (linear).

The slope of the velocity-time graph gives the acceleration, and the area under it gives the displacement.

Therefore, the statement 'Velocity-time graph is non-linear' is incorrect.

Answer: Velocity-time graph is non-linear.

72342.subject: Physics
72342.text: The bob of simple pendulum performs S.H.M. with a frequency $'n'$ in air and with frequency $'n_1'$ in water. If the density of the material of bob is $'x'$ g / cc and the ratio $n / n_1$ is 3, then density of bob $'x'$ is ( density of water $= 1$ g /cc and neglect friction due to water)
72342.sol:
The frequency of a simple pendulum in air is given by $n = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{l}}$.

When the bob is immersed in water, the effective acceleration due to gravity becomes $g' = g \left(1 - \dfrac{\rho_{water}}{\rho_{bob}} \right).

Given $\rho_{water} = 1$ g/cc and $\rho_{bob} = x$ g/cc, we have $g' = g $\left( 1 - \dfrac{1}{x} \right) = g \left( \dfrac{x - 1}{x} \right).

The frequency$ of the pendulum in water is n_1 = $\dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{g'}{l}}.

The ratio of the frequencies is \dfrac{n}{n_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{g'}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{x}{x - 1}}.

Given \dfrac{n}{n_1} =3$, we get \sqrt{$\dfrac{x}{x - 1}}$=$3$.

Squaring both sides, $\dfrac{x}{x - 1} =9$.

$x = 9x - 9$

8x = 9 \Rightarrow x = $\dfrac{9}{8}$g/cc.

Answer: $\dfrac{9}{8}$

73881.subject: General Ability
73881.text: Why a fielder in the ground gradually pulls his hands backward while catching a fast moving cricket ball?
options: To reduce the acceleration of the ball
To increase the acceleration of the ball
To increase the velocity of the ball
73881.sol:
When a fielder pulls his hands backward while catching a fast-moving cricket ball, the time taken to bring the ball to rest is increased.

Since acceleration is the rate of change of velocity ($a = \dfrac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$), increasing the time interval $\Delta t$ decreases the magnitude of acceleration.

According to Newton's second law of motion ($F = ma$), a smaller acceleration results in a smaller impact force exerted on the fielder's hands, thereby preventing injury.

Therefore, the fielder pulls his hands backward to reduce the acceleration of the ball.

Answer: To reduce the acceleration of the ball

77843.subject: Mathematics
77843.text:
For the following two (02) items:
There are 8 points on a plane out of which 4 points are collinear.

How many quadrilaterals can be formed by joining these points?
77843.sol:
Total number of points is $8$.

Number of collinear points is $4$.

Total number of ways to select $4$ points from $8$ points is ^{8}C_{4} = 70$.

A quadrilateral cannot be formed if 3$ or $4$ selected points are collinear.

Number of ways to select $4$ collinear points is ^{4}C_{4} = 1$.

Number of ways to select 3$ collinear points and $1$ non-collinear point is ^{4}C_{3} \times ^{4}C_{1} = 4 \times 4 = 16$.

Total number of quadrilaterals that can be formed is 70 - (1 + 16) = 53$.

Answer: $53$

78512.subject: Mathematics
78512.text: Let two lines of regression be $x+y+11=0$ and $2x+3y+4=0$ for some data. What is the value of correlation coefficient between $x$ and $y$ ?
78512.sol:
Let the regression line of $y$ on $x$ be $2x+3y+4=0$.

$3y = -2x - 4 \Rightarrow y = -\dfrac{2}{3}x - \dfrac{4}{3}$

The regression coefficient of $y$ on $x$ is $b_{yx} = -\dfrac{2}{3}$.

Let the regression line of $x$ on $y$ be $x+y+11=0$.

$x = -y - 11$

The regression coefficient of $x$ on $y$ is $b_{xy} = -1$.

The square of the correlation coefficient is given by $r^2 = b_{yx} \times b_{xy}$.

$r^2 = \left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right) \times (-1) = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Since $r^2 \le 1$, our assumption for the regression lines is correct. Furthermore, since both regression coefficients $b_{yx}$ and $b_{xy}$ are negative, the correlation coefficient $r$ must also be negative.

$r = -\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$

Answer: $-\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$

83476.subject: Physics
83476.text: A thin horizontal disc is rotating about a vertical axis passing through its fixed centre $O$. Its angular momentum is $L_A$ and $L_B$ computed about points $A$ and $B$, respectively, with $OB=2\times OA$. The value of $\dfrac{L_A}{L_B}$ is :
83476.sol:
The angular momentum of a rigid body about any arbitrary point $P$ is given by the relation:

$\vec{L}_P = \vec{L}_{cm} + \vec{r}_{cm/P} \times M\vec{v}_{cm}$

where $\vec{L}_{cm}$ is the angular momentum of the body about its center of mass, $\vec{r}_{cm/P}$ is the position vector of the center of mass with respect to point $P$, $M$ is the total mass of the body, and $\vec{v}_{cm}$ is the velocity of the center of mass.

In the given problem, the disc is rotating about a vertical axis passing through its fixed center $O$. Since the center of mass of the disc is at $O$ and is fixed, its velocity is zero, i.e., $\vec{v}_{cm} = 0$.

Substituting $\vec{v}_{cm} = 0$ into the angular momentum equation, we get:

$\vec{L}_P = \vec{L}_{cm} + \vec{r}_{cm/P} \times 0$

$\vec{L}_P = \vec{L}_{cm}$

This shows that the angular momentum of the disc is independent of the choice of the reference point and is equal to its angular momentum about the center of mass.

Therefore, the angular momentum about point $A$ is equal to the angular momentum about point $B$:

$L_A = L_B = L_{cm}$

Hence, the ratio is:

$\dfrac{L_A}{L_B} = 1$

Answer: $1$

83657.subject: Physics
83657.text: An electric heater supplies heat to a system at a rate of $100$ W. If the system performs work at a rate of $75$ J/s, then the rate at which internal energy increases will be :
83657.sol:
According to the first law of thermodynamics:

$\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = \dfrac{dU}{dt} + \dfrac{dW}{dt}$

Given that the rate of heat supplied is $\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = 100$ W and the rate of work done by the system is $\dfrac{dW}{dt} = 75$ J/s = $75$ W.

Substituting the values:

$100 = \dfrac{dU}{dt} + 75$

$\dfrac{dU}{dt} = 100 - 75 = 25$ W

The rate at which internal energy increases is $25$ W.

Answer: $25$ W

91627.text: The probability of an event $A$ is $\dfrac{4}{5} .$ The probability of an event $B,$ given that the event $A$ occurs is $\dfrac{1}{5}.$ The probability of event $A$, given that the event $B$ occurs is $\dfrac{2}{3} .$ The probability that neither of the events occurs is
91627.sol:
$P\left(A\right) = \dfrac{4}{5}, P\left(\dfrac{B}{A}\right) = \dfrac{P\left(A \cap B\right)}{P\left(A\right)} = \dfrac{1}{5} ⇒ P\left(A \cap B\right) = \dfrac{4}{25}$

$P\left(\dfrac{A}{B}\right) = \dfrac{P\left(A \cap B\right)}{P\left(B\right)} = \dfrac{2}{3} ⇒ P\left(B\right) = \dfrac{4}{25} \times \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{6}{25}$

$P\left(A^{c} \cap B^{c}\right) = P{ \left(A \cup B\right)}^{c} = 1 - P \left(A \cup B\right) = 1 - P \left(A\right) - P\left(B\right) + P\left(A \cap B\right)$

$= 1 - \dfrac{4}{5} - \dfrac{6}{25} + \dfrac{4}{25} = \dfrac{3}{25}$

93248.text:
A cord of length $h = 64m$ is used to connect an astronaut (m = 100kg$) to a spaceship (M ≫ m$) which is orbiting near the earth's surface as shown in the figure. Assuming& that the spaceship and the astronaut fall on a straight line from the earth's centre, then the tension in the cord is close to [R = 6400km$] \text{ and }

$
93248.sol:
According to given problem, the mass of satellite $M$ is much greater than that of astronaut $m$. So the centre of mass of the system will be close to satellite and as the satellite is orbiting close to the surface of earth, the equation of motion of the system $( S + A )$ will be-

$\dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{e ⁡}\left(M ⁡ + m ⁡\right)}{R{⁡}^{2}} = \left(M ⁡ + m ⁡\right)R ⁡ {\omega}^{2}$

i.e., $R ⁡ {\omega}^{2} = \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{e ⁡}}{R{⁡}^{2}} = \text{g} \ldots \left(\text{i}\right)$

And the equation of motion of the astronaut will be

$\dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{e ⁡}m ⁡}{r{⁡}^{2}} + T ⁡ = m ⁡ r ⁡ {\omega}^{2}\text{,}\text{i.e.,}T ⁡ = m ⁡ \left[r ⁡ {\omega}^{2} - \dfrac{{\text{GM}}_{e ⁡}}{r{⁡}^{2}}\right]$

In the light of equation (i), above equation reduces to

$T ⁡ = \text{mg}\left[\dfrac{r ⁡}{R ⁡} - {\left(\dfrac{R ⁡}{r ⁡}\right)}^{2}\right] = \text{mg}\left[\dfrac{\left(R ⁡ + h ⁡\right)}{R ⁡} - \dfrac{R{⁡}^{2}}{{\left(R ⁡ + h ⁡\right)}^{2}}\right]$

                          $\left[\text{as}r ⁡ = R ⁡ + h ⁡\right]$

or   $T ⁡ = \text{mg}\left[\left(1 + \dfrac{h ⁡}{R ⁡}\right) - {\left(1 + \dfrac{h ⁡}{R ⁡}\right)}^{- 2}\right] = \dfrac{3\text{mgh}}{R ⁡}$

                          $\left[\text{as}{\left(1 + \dfrac{h ⁡}{R ⁡}\right)}^{- 2} ⋍ 1 - \dfrac{2h ⁡}{R ⁡}\right]$

So substituting the given data,

                 $T ⁡ = \dfrac{3 \times 100 \times 10 \times 64}{6400 \times {10}^{3}} = 3 \times {10}^{- 2}\text{N}$

93861.sol:
Suppose they meet $x$ hours after 7 a.m.

Distance covered by A in $x$ hours = 20$x$ km.

Distance covered by B in $( x – 1 )$ hours $= 25 ( x – 1 ) km$

$20x + 25 ( x - 1 ) = 110$

$45x = 135 ⇒ x = 3 hr$

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{19 \times 9.8 \times 1.5}{10}} = \sqrt{27.93} = 5.285ms^{- 1}$

$v = 5 .3 ms^{- 1}$

95725.text: In the given options, there is a property of a group and a representative example following that property. Which of these is incorrect?
options: All prokaryotes classified under kingdom Monera have cell wall (Mycoplasma)

All prions don't have nucleic acid as their genetic material (Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy Prion)

95725.sol: The Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen. Many mycoplasma are pathogenic in animals and plants. Viroids are smaller than viruses and cause potato spindle tuber disease. It was found to be a free RNA; it lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses, hence the name viroid. The RNA of the viroid was of low molecular weight. In modern medicine certain infectious neurological diseases were found to be transmitted by an agent consisting of abnormally folded protein. The agent was similar in size to viruses. These agents were called prions. The most notable diseases caused by prions are bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) commonly called mad cow disease in cattle.

100688.subject: Physics
100688.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a block of mass $m$ is placed on a rough inclined plane of angle $\theta$ such that $\tan \theta < \mu_s$ (where $\mu_s$ is the coefficient of static friction), the net force on the block is zero.
Reason (R): The limiting value of static friction is directly proportional to the normal reaction acting on the block.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
100688.sol:
For Assertion (A): The condition $\tan \theta < \mu_s$ implies that the angle of inclination $\theta$ is less than the angle of repose. In this condition, the component of weight along the incline ($mg \sin \theta$) is less than the limiting static friction ($\mu_s mg \cos \theta$). The block will not slide and remains in static equilibrium. Hence, the net force on the block is zero. Assertion (A) is correct.

For Reason (R): The limiting value of static friction is indeed directly proportional to the normal reaction ($f_{s,\text{max}} = \mu_s N$). Reason (R) is a correct statement.

However, Reason (R) alone does not explain Assertion (A). The correct explanation for (A) is that static friction is a self-adjusting force that balances the applied force ($mg \sin \theta$) when the block is not on the verge of sliding. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

100993.subject: Physics
100993.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
100993.text:
Two particles mass \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) are kept at rest at \(t=0\). They start attracting each other due to their gravitational pull, then
Statement-I: The total momentum of the system is zero at any instant.
Statement-II: Both the particles gain equal momentum in opposite direction in equal interval of time as both are acted upon equal and opposite forces.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct.
100993.sol:
1. By Newton's third law the internal forces are equal and opposite:
\(\mathrm{F}_{12}=-\mathrm{F}_{21} .\)
If \(\mathrm{p}_1, \mathrm{p}_2\) are momenta, then
\(\frac{d \mathrm{p}_1}{d t}=\mathrm{F}_{12}, \quad \frac{d \mathrm{p}_2}{d t}=\mathrm{F}_{21}=-\mathrm{F}_{12} .\)
Add them:
\(\frac{d}{d t}\left(\mathrm{p}_1+\mathrm{p}_2\right)=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{p}_1+\mathrm{p}_2=\text{ constant }\)
Initially both particles are at rest, so \(\mathrm{p}_1+\mathrm{p}_2=\mathrm{0}\). Hence at every later time the total momentum remains zero. This proves Statement I.
2. From the pair of equations above,
\(\frac{d \mathrm{p}_1}{d t}=-\frac{d \mathrm{p}_2}{d t} .\)
Integrating over any equal time interval gives
\(\Delta \mathrm{p}_1=-\Delta \mathrm{p}_2,\)
i.e. they gain equal magnitude momenta in opposite directions (even though their velocities will be different if \(m_1 \neq m_2\)). That proves Statement II.
Both statements are therefore true (and Statement II \(\downarrow\) ist the differential form of the same Newton-third law fact that ensures Statement J).

102402.subject: Physics
102402.text: A simple pendulum has a time period $T$ when oscillating in air. When the pendulum bob is completely immersed in water, its time period becomes $\sqrt{2}T$. If the density of water is $1000 \text{ kg/m}^3$ and viscous forces are neglected, the density of the material of the pendulum bob is
102402.sol:
The time period of a simple pendulum in air is given by:
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$

When immersed in a liquid, the effective acceleration due to gravity $g_{eff}$ is reduced due to buoyancy:
$g_{eff} = g \left(1 - \dfrac{\rho_w}{\rho_b}\right)$
where $\rho_w$ is the density of water and $\rho_b$ is the density of the bob.

The new time period is:
$T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g_{eff}}}$

Given that $T' = \sqrt{2}T$, we have:
$2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g_{eff}}} = \sqrt{2} \left(2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}\right)$

Squaring both sides:
$\dfrac{l}{g_{eff}} = 2 \left(\dfrac{l}{g}\right)$
$g_{eff} = \dfrac{g}{2}$

Equating this to the expression for $g_{eff}$:
$g \left(1 - \dfrac{\rho_w}{\rho_b}\right) = \dfrac{g}{2}$
$1 - \dfrac{1000}{\rho_b} = \dfrac{1}{2}$
$\dfrac{1000}{\rho_b} = \dfrac{1}{2}$
$\rho_b = 2000 \text{ kg/m}^3$

Using the inverted density ratio would incorrectly yield $500 \text{ kg/m}^3$, and forgetting to square the time period ratio leads to an incorrect irrational density.

Answer: $2000 \text{ kg/m}^3$

103847.subject: Physics
103847.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : A time varying magnetic field induces an electric field.
Reason (R) : An inductor always tends to keep the flux constant.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
103847.sol:
- Assertion (A) states that a time-varying magnetic field induces an electric field. This is a direct consequence of Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction, which states that a changing magnetic flux (often due to a time-varying magnetic field) induces an electromotive force (EMF), and this EMF is associated with an induced electric field. So, Assertion (A) is true.
- Reason (R) states that an inductor always tends to keep the flux constant. While inductors do oppose changes in current (and thus changes in magnetic flux through them) according to Lenz's Law, they do not always keep the flux constant. The flux changes to induce an EMF, and the inductor's role is to oppose this change. If the current is changing, the flux is also changing. So, Reason (R) is false.
Since Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false, the most appropriate answer is (3).
The correct option is (3).

103855.subject: Physics
103855.text:
The diagram below shows two circle loops of wire (A and B) centred on and perpendicular to the $\mathrm{x}$-axis, and oriented with their planes parallel to each other. The $y$-axis passes vertically through loop A (dashed line). There is a current $I_{B}$ in loop B as shown. Possible actions which we might perform on loop A are:
(i) Move A to the right along $x$ axis closer to $B$ (ii) Move A to the left along $x$ axis away from B (iii) As viewed from above, rotate A clockwise about y axis (iv) As viewed from above, rotate A anticlockwise about y axis Which of these actions will induce a current in A only in the direction shown.
103855.sol:
When we move loop A to the right, closer to loop B, the magnetic flux through loop A increases. According to Lenz's Law, the induced current will create a magnetic field to oppose this increase. Since loop B's current (\(I_B\)) creates a magnetic field that points to the right (inside the loop) based on the right-hand rule, the induced current in loop A must create a magnetic field pointing to the left to oppose it. For loop A to create a magnetic field pointing to the left, the induced current must flow in the direction shown, which is counter-clockwise as viewed from the positive x-axis. Thus, moving A to the right induces a current in the direction shown.
When we move loop A to the left, away from loop B, the magnetic flux through loop A decreases. The induced current will again oppose this change. The induced magnetic field must now point to the right, in the same direction as the original field from loop B, to counteract the decrease in flux. This requires the induced current to flow in the opposite direction from the one shown. Therefore, moving A to the left does not induce a current in the direction shown.
Rotating loop A about the y-axis (either clockwise or counter-clockwise) while keeping its center on the x-axis does not change the amount of magnetic flux passing through it. This is because the magnetic field lines from loop B are primarily parallel to the x -axis near the center of loop A. Since the magnetic flux remains constant, no current is induced.
Based on the analysis, only action (i), moving loop A to the right along the x-axis, will induce a current in the direction shown.

105420.subject: Physics
105420.text: A screw gauge has a pitch of $0.5\text{ mm}$ and $50$ divisions on its circular scale. When used to measure the thickness of a glass plate, the main scale reading is $2.0\text{ mm}$ and the total measured thickness is $2.34\text{ mm}$. The reading on the circular scale (number of coinciding divisions) is:
105420.sol:
Least count (LC) of the screw gauge is given by:
$\text{LC} = \dfrac{\text{Pitch}}{\text{Number of circular scale divisions}}$
$\text{LC} = \dfrac{0.5\text{ mm}}{50} = 0.01\text{ mm}$

The total reading is given by the formula:
$\text{Total Reading} = \text{Main Scale Reading (MSR)} + (\text{Circular Scale Reading (CSR)} \times \text{LC})$

Substituting the given values:
$2.34\text{ mm} = 2.0\text{ mm} + (\text{CSR} \times 0.01\text{ mm})$
$0.34\text{ mm} = \text{CSR} \times 0.01\text{ mm}$

$\text{CSR} = \dfrac{0.34}{0.01} = 34$

The coinciding division on the circular scale is $34$.

Answer: $34$

Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
107550.sol:
The oxidation state of $+ 5$ in pentahalides is more covalent as compared to the $+ 3$ oxidation state in trihalides. Due to the higher positive oxidation state of the central atom in pentahalide state, these atoms will have larger polarising power than the halogen atom attached to them since the polarising power is directly proportional to the charge. More is the polarisation, larger will be the covalent character of the bond. Hence, due to larger polarisation of bond in pentahalide state as compared to trihalide state, the ${SbCl}_{5}$ is more covalent than ${SbCl}_{3}$. 

Higher oxides of halogens are more stable than lower ones due to the formation of more number of bonds, which results in higher release of energy. So, both the statements I and II are correct.

108678.subject: Chemistry
108678.text:
An ideal gas at $400\text{ K}$ expands isothermally from $1.0\text{ L}$ to $4.0\text{ L}$ against a constant external pressure of $2.0\text{ bar}$. The heat absorbed ($q$) by the gas in this process is:

(Given: $1\text{ L bar} = 100\text{ J}$)
108678.sol:
The work done by the gas against a constant external pressure is:
$W = -P_{\text{ext}}(V_{f} - V_{i})$

$W = -2.0 \times (4.0 - 1.0) = -6.0\text{ L bar}$

Converting to Joules:
$W = -6.0 \times 100 = -600\text{ J}$

For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process, the change in internal energy is zero ($\Delta U = 0$).

According to the first law of thermodynamics:
$\Delta U = q + W$

$0 = q + (-600)$

$q = +600\text{ J}$

Thus, the heat absorbed by the gas is $+600\text{ J}$.

Answer: $+600\text{ J}$

108688.subject: Chemistry
108688.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For one mole of an ideal gas, the molar heat capacity at constant volume ($C_v$) is greater than the molar heat capacity at constant pressure ($C_p$) by an amount $R$.
Reason (R): Heating a gas at constant pressure requires additional heat to do work of expansion against the external pressure.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
108688.sol:
Assertion (A) is false because for an ideal gas, the molar heat capacity at constant pressure ($C_p$) is greater than the molar heat capacity at constant volume ($C_v$) by the universal gas constant $R$ (i.e., $C_p - C_v = R$, not $C_v - C_p = R$).

Reason (R) is true. When a gas is heated at constant volume, no expansion work is done, and all the heat supplied increases the internal energy. However, when heated at constant pressure, the gas expands and does work against the external pressure. Therefore, extra heat must be supplied to achieve the same rise in temperature, which is the physical reason why $C_p > C_v$.

Thus, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

114352.subject: Chemistry
114352.text:
The conductivity and resistance of four different conductivity cells (P, Q, R, and S) filled with the same electrolyte solution are given in the table below. Assuming the area of cross-section of the electrodes is identical for all the cells, which cell has the maximum distance between its electrodes?

CellConductivity ($\kappa$) / $\text{S cm}^{-1}$Resistance ($R$) / $\Omega$
P$0.05$$20$
Q$0.01$$150$
R$0.02$$90$
S$0.04$$10$
114352.sol:
The cell constant ($G^*$) of a conductivity cell is given by the relation:
$G^* = \dfrac{l}{a} = \kappa \times R$

Since the area of cross-section ($a$) is constant for all cells, the distance between the electrodes ($l$) is directly proportional to the product of conductivity ($\kappa$) and resistance ($R$).

Calculating $\kappa \times R$ for each cell:
For Cell P: $G^* = 0.05 \times 20 = 1.0 \text{ cm}^{-1}$
For Cell Q: $G^* = 0.01 \times 150 = 1.5 \text{ cm}^{-1}$
For Cell R: $G^* = 0.02 \times 90 = 1.8 \text{ cm}^{-1}$
For Cell S: $G^* = 0.04 \times 10 = 0.4 \text{ cm}^{-1}$

Cell R has the maximum value of the cell constant, which means it has the maximum distance between its electrodes.

Answer: Cell R

114871.subject: Chemistry
114871.text:
For a chemical reaction, the plot of $\ln[\text{R}]$ versus time $t$ yields a straight line with a slope of $-0.02 \text{ s}^{-1}$. How much time will it take for the concentration of the reactant to drop from $0.8 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$ to $0.1 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$?
(Given : $\ln 2 = 0.693$, $\log 2 = 0.301$)
114871.sol:
For a first-order reaction, the integrated rate equation is:
$\ln[\text{R}] = -kt + \ln[\text{R}]_0$
The plot of $\ln[\text{R}]$ versus $t$ is a straight line with slope $= -k$.
Given slope $= -0.02 \text{ s}^{-1}$, we have $k = 0.02 \text{ s}^{-1}$.

The half-life of the reaction is:
$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{\ln 2}{k} = \dfrac{0.693}{0.02} = 34.65 \text{ s}$

The concentration drops from $0.8 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$ to $0.1 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$, which is a reduction to $\dfrac{1}{8}$ of the initial amount.
This corresponds to 3 half-lives ($2^3 = 8$).

Total time $t = 3 \times t_{1/2} = 3 \times 34.65 = 103.95 \text{ s}$.

Using the zero-order formula gives $35.0 \text{ s}$, and misinterpreting the slope as $-k/2.303$ gives $45.15 \text{ s}$, both of which are incorrect.

Answer: $103.95 \text{ s}$

123711.subject: Botany
123711.text: What is the result of the process described in Telophase II in meiosis?
options: The formation of two haploid cells
The reappearance of the nuclear envelope
The formation of four haploid daughter cells
123711.sol: Prophase II: Meiosis II is initiated immediately after cytokinesis, usually before the chromosomes have fully elongated. In contrast to meiosis I, meiosis II resembles a normal mitosis. The nuclear membrane disappears by the end of prophase II (Figure 10.4). The chromosomes again become compact. Metaphase II: At this stage the chromosomes align at the equator and the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle get attached to the kinetochores (Figure 10.4) of sister chromatids. Meiosis ends with telophase II, in which the two groups of chromosomes once again get enclosed by a nuclear envelope; cytokinesis follows resulting in the formation of tetrad of cells i.e., four haploid daughter cells.

123883.subject: Botany
123883.text:
A cell is observed under a microscope during division. The chromosomes are found to be aligned at the equator of the cell. It is specifically noted that spindle fibres from one pole are attached to the kinetochore of one entire chromosome (consisting of two sister chromatids), while spindle fibres from the opposite pole are attached to the kinetochore of its homologous partner.

Identify the specific stage of cell division described above.
123883.sol:
In Metaphase I of meiosis, the bivalent chromosomes align on the equatorial plate. The microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle attach to the kinetochores of homologous chromosomes. This means each entire chromosome (with its two sister chromatids) is attached to only one pole.

In contrast, during mitotic metaphase and metaphase II of meiosis, spindle fibres from opposite poles attach to the kinetochores of sister chromatids of the same chromosome.

Anaphase I involves the actual movement of these homologous chromosomes to the opposite poles, not their alignment at the equator.

Therefore, the described stage is Metaphase I of meiosis.

Answer: Metaphase I of meiosis
